info.title: Academic Success Platform API
info.description: Backend API for the Academic Success Platform. Provides student management, GPA tracking, AI-powered recommendations, and course workload analysis.

post.description:
Create a new student account and return a fresh token pair.

Delegates to ``create_user`` which raises **400** if the e-mail is already
registered.  On success, the response includes both an access token and a
refresh token so the client can start making authenticated requests
immediately without a separate login call.

Args:
    data: Validated registration payload (email, password, name, major, …).
    db: Injected async database session.

Returns:
    :class:`~app.schemas.user.TokenResponse` with the access token, refresh
    token, and the new user's serialised profile.

Raises:
    HTTPException: 400 ``"Email already registered"`` — raised by
        ``create_user`` when the e-mail violates the unique constraint.

201.description: JWT token pair and serialised user profile.

post.summary: Authenticate and receive a JWT token pair
post.description:
Verify credentials and return a fresh access + refresh token pair.

Returns the same **401** for both "unknown e-mail" and "wrong password"
to prevent user enumeration.

Args:
    data: Login payload containing ``email`` and ``password``.
    db: Injected async database session.

Returns:
    :class:`~app.schemas.user.TokenResponse` with the access token, refresh
    token, and the authenticated user's serialised profile.

Raises:
    HTTPException: 401 ``"Invalid email or password"`` — raised when
        credentials are invalid or the account does not exist.

200.description: JWT token pair and serialised user profile.

post.description:
OAuth2-compatible token endpoint that accepts form-encoded credentials.

This endpoint exists solely to satisfy the ``OAuth2PasswordBearer`` scheme
used by Swagger UI's **Authorize** dialog, which always POSTs
``application/x-www-form-urlencoded`` with ``username`` and ``password``
fields.  The ``username`` field is treated as the student's e-mail address.

For programmatic API access prefer ``POST /api/auth/login`` with a JSON
body instead.

Args:
    form: Standard OAuth2 password request form (``username`` = email,
        ``password`` = plain-text password).
    db: Injected async database session.

Returns:
    :class:`~app.schemas.user.TokenResponse` with the access token, refresh
    token, and the authenticated user's serialised profile.

Raises:
    HTTPException: 401 ``"Invalid email or password"`` — credentials are
        wrong or the account does not exist.

200.description: JWT token pair and serialised user profile.

post.summary: Rotate tokens using a valid refresh token
post.description:
Issue a new access + refresh token pair from a valid refresh token.

The old refresh token is consumed (clients must store the new one).
The ``type`` claim in the token is enforced by ``verify_refresh_token`` —
presenting an access token here will be rejected even if it is otherwise
valid.

Args:
    data: Body containing the ``refresh_token`` string.
    db: Injected async database session.

Returns:
    :class:`~app.schemas.user.TokenResponse` with a fresh access token,
    new refresh token, and the user's serialised profile.

Raises:
    HTTPException: 401 when the token is invalid, expired, wrong type, or
        the associated user no longer exists or is inactive.

200.description: New JWT token pair and serialised user profile.
Serialised profile of the currently authenticated student.

patch.description:
Partially update the authenticated user's mutable profile fields.

Only ``name``, ``major``, ``level``, ``university``, and
``total_credit_hours`` may be changed. Identity fields (``id``, ``email``)
and ``created_at`` are immutable and are silently ignored even if they
appear in the request body.

Send only the fields you want to change — omitted fields are left
untouched.

Args:
    data: Partial profile payload (all fields optional).
    db: Injected async database session.
    current_user: Authenticated user resolved from the Bearer token.

Returns:
    :class:`~app.schemas.user.UserResponse` — the full serialised profile
    of the user after the update.

Raises:
    HTTPException: 401 for a missing or invalid Bearer token.

200.description: Updated serialised profile of the currently authenticated student.

post.description:
Generate a short-lived password-reset token for the given e-mail address.

**Always returns HTTP 200** regardless of whether the e-mail is registered
— this prevents user-enumeration attacks.  When the account exists, a UUID
token is stored in Redis with a 15-minute TTL and returned in the response
body so the mobile client can construct a deep-link or pass it directly to
``POST /api/auth/reset-password``.

In a production deployment the token would be e-mailed rather than returned
in the response.  Returning it here is intentional for the mobile-first
development workflow where the app handles the reset link itself.

Args:
    data: Body containing the ``email`` field.
    db: Injected async database session.

Returns:
    :class:`~app.schemas.user.ForgotPasswordResponse` with a
    ``message`` string and a ``reset_token`` (empty string when the
    e-mail is unknown).

200.description: Confirmation message and a one-time reset token. reset_token is an empty string when the e-mail is not registered.

post.summary: Reset password using a valid reset token
post.description:
Consume a one-time reset token and update the user's password.

The token must have been issued by ``POST /api/auth/forgot-password`` and
must not be expired (15-minute TTL) or already consumed.  After a
successful reset the token is permanently deleted from Redis and cannot be
reused.

After resetting, the user must log in again with the new password via
``POST /api/auth/login`` — any existing access/refresh tokens remain
valid until their natural expiry but the client should discard them.

Args:
    data: Body containing ``token`` and ``new_password``.
    db: Injected async database session.

Returns:
    :class:`~app.schemas.user.MessageResponse` confirming the update.

Raises:
    HTTPException: 400 ``"Invalid or expired reset token"`` when the
        token is not found in Redis (expired, consumed, or never issued).

200.description: Confirmation that the password was updated successfully.

post.summary: Signal session logout (client must discard tokens)
post.description:
Signal a session logout for the authenticated user.

JWT tokens are stateless and cannot be server-side invalidated without a
token blacklist (not implemented at this stage).  This endpoint serves as
a formal contract point for the mobile client — upon receiving the 200
response the client **must** discard both its access token and refresh
token from local storage.

Requiring a valid Bearer token ensures this endpoint is not callable
anonymously and provides an audit log entry for the logout event.

Args:
    current_user: Authenticated user resolved from the Bearer token.

Returns:
    :class:`~app.schemas.user.MessageResponse` with
    ``"Logged out successfully."``.

Raises:
    HTTPException: 401 for a missing or invalid Bearer token.

200.description: Confirmation that the logout was acknowledged.

delete.description:
Soft-delete the authenticated user account.

The user's `is_active` flag is set to False. They will no longer be able
to log in or access protected endpoints. All data (courses, GPA, chat
history, etc.) remains intact in the database.

Args:
    db: Injected async database session.
    current_user: Authenticated user resolved from the Bearer token.

Returns:
    HTTP 204 No Content.

Raises:
    HTTPException: 401 for a missing or invalid Bearer token.

post.summary: Post a message to a conversation (streaming SSE)
post.description:
Stream an AI reply into a conversation via Server-Sent Events.

- Saves the user message and the completed AI reply to ``chat_history``.
- Bumps ``conversations.updated_at`` after the stream finishes.
- Respects the same daily rate-limit as all other AI endpoints.

200.description: A text/event-stream of JSON objects: {"token": "...", "done": false} … {"token": "", "done": true}

get.description:
Return the preference fields stored on the authenticated user's account.

These fields are also included in the full ``UserResponse`` returned by
``GET /api/auth/me``, but this endpoint exists as a dedicated, lightweight
alternative for clients that only need preference data.

Args:
    current_user: Authenticated user resolved from the Bearer token.

Returns:
    :class:`~app.schemas.user.UserPreferencesResponse` — the five
    preference fields (may be ``null`` if not yet set).

Raises:
    HTTPException: 401 for a missing or invalid Bearer token.

200.description: Serialised preference fields for the currently authenticated student.

put.description:
Partially update the authenticated user's preference fields.

All fields are optional — send only what needs to change.  Fields omitted
from the request body are left untouched (partial-update / PATCH semantics
even though the verb is ``PUT`` for idiomatic REST resource replacement
intent).

Args:
    data: Preference payload (all fields optional).
    db: Injected async database session.
    current_user: Authenticated user resolved from the Bearer token.

Returns:
    :class:`~app.schemas.user.UserPreferencesResponse` — the five
    preference fields after the update.

Raises:
    HTTPException: 401 for a missing or invalid Bearer token.

200.description: Serialised preference fields after the update.

get.description:
Retrieve all academic achievements and the user's progress for each.

Achievements are returned ordered by category, then by title. Progress is
computed dynamically on each request (0-100%).

200.description: Full catalog of achievements with the student's dynamic progress.
Returns the service status and current runtime environment.
